summary: create_push_descriptor_resources() now declares the vertex push-constant range only when r->use_push_constants_for_uniform_attrs && n > 0, mirroring create_pipeline()'s guard, and the flag is computed at the top of pgraph_vk_init_shaders() before any consumer.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- a device reporting maxPushConstantsSize == 256 building a {VERTEX, offset 16, size 256} range that ends at 272 for n = 16 -- can no longer occur. want_vtx_range is false exactly when the flag is false, and the flag is false exactly when maxPushConstantsSize < GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE + MAX_UNIFORM_ATTR_VALUES_SIZE = 16 + 256 = 272. So no layout carrying the vertex range is ever created on a device that cannot hold it.
evidence: Guard equivalence checked against the other side rather than assumed: create_pipeline() (draw.c:2290) adds the range iff use_push_constants_for_uniform_attrs && __builtin_popcount(uniform_attrs) != 0; push_template_index() (draw.c:2526) returns popcount when the flag is true and 0 when it is false. Template n is therefore selected exactly for a pipeline with n uniform attributes, and both sides agree for every n including the flag-false case (both declare 1 range). Ordering verified independently: device_props is written only at instance.c:581/610, and pgraph_vk_init_instance() runs at renderer.c:187 against pgraph_vk_init_shaders() at renderer.c:229. grep for use_push_constants_for_uniform_attrs shows the only other readers are draw.c (per-draw) and shaders.c:833 (shader_binding_build_module_keys); neither is reached by any init step between the new computation point and create_push_descriptor_resources(). shader_cache_init()'s warmup replays ShaderModuleCacheKey blobs read from shader_module_keys.bin and does not rebuild keys, so moving the flag before it changes nothing there. Only create_push_descriptor_resources() and create_pipeline() build a layout carrying this range: display.c:589 is fragment-stage, surface-compute.c:305/938 are compute.
remediation: None required. The second bug the remediation found -- the flag being computed at line 1435 after create_push_descriptor_resources() ran at 1416, against a g_malloc0'd PGRAPHVkState -- is correctly fixed by moving the computation rather than by gating alone.
note: One claim in the fix is weaker than stated. The assert at shaders.c:328 (push_ranges[1].offset + push_ranges[1].size <= maxPushConstantsSize) is implied by the flag it sits under: offset is GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE and size is at most MAX_UNIFORM_ATTR_VALUES_SIZE, which is exactly the sum the flag tests. It can never fire. The commit message says it 'makes the next offset change fail loudly here'; that is true only for a change that moves the vertex offset to something other than GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE. A change made through GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE -- the likely shape, since both sides use it -- moves the flag's threshold in lockstep and the assert stays tautological. This does not weaken the fix, which rests on the gate, not the assert.

summary: Both halves landed. The geometry push is no longer gated on pipeline_changed, and check_draw_mergeable() now compares line width.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- two line draws in one reorder window with identical pipeline state and different SET_LINE_WIDTH -- can no longer occur on either route. Push half: the second entry has has_dynamic_line_width true, prev has it true, e->line_width differs, so width_changed is true and vkCmdPushConstants is issued. Merge half: the two draws no longer reach one draw call at all, because check_draw_mergeable() returns false on pg->line_width != q->line_width.
evidence: Verified that the new DrawQueue field is initialised at every activation site, not only the ones the diff touched: all four `q->active = true` sites (draw.c:4670, 4780, 6069, 6126) are immediately preceded by `q->line_width = pg->line_width` (4669, 4779, 6066, 6123); the fifth `active = true` at 6006 is `w->active` on ReorderWindow, a different struct. Types match exactly -- pg->line_width is uint32_t (pgraph.h:271) and DrawQueue::line_width is uint32_t (renderer.h:1001), so the comparison is on the raw 1/8-px register with no conversion; ReorderWindowEntry::line_width is a separate float in guest px (renderer.h:1047), used only for the push. The justification for a new field rather than an existing generation counter was checked at the source: DEF_METHOD(NV097, SET_LINE_WIDTH) (pgraph.c:3045-3055) assigns pg->line_width directly, writes no register and bumps no generation, so every existing member of the comparison set is genuinely blind to it.
remediation: None required.
note: Two side effects of the fix that pass 1 could not have seen, neither a defect. (1) The push moved out of the `if (pipeline_changed)` block, and the uncompiled-pipeline early return (`e->pipeline_binding->pipeline == VK_NULL_HANDLE`) is inside that block. So when an entry is skipped for an uncompiled pipeline and the caller sets prev = e unconditionally (draw.c:5897-5898), a following entry with the same binding now issues a vkCmdPushConstants where it previously issued none. e->layout is still a valid VkPipelineLayout in that case (assigned at draw.c:5527 from a binding that is never NULL), and vkCmdPushConstants does not require a bound pipeline, so this is a wasted call, not an invalid one. The underlying problem -- that such an entry proceeds to draw with no pipeline bound -- is pre-existing and unchanged by this commit. (2) The merge check is unconditional rather than line-primitive-only, which the comment states as a deliberate choice. A title that writes SET_LINE_WIDTH between triangle draws now loses draw merging where it did not before. That is a throughput cost, not a correctness one, and the comment's reasoning for preferring it is sound.

summary: Correctly out of lane.remediate1's scope: target/** is lane.remote's territory in territory.toml wave 39. The routing is recorded in four places. It has not, however, been delivered to lane.remote.
scenario: Not verified as closed, and not expected to be -- no code change was made. Confirmed NOT silently dropped: territory.toml line 63 ([lane.remediate1].note) states 'M2 (fpu_helper.c) and M4 (gl/texture.c) are NOT here: both are lane.remote's territory and are routed there'; commit 4b349edd82 says the same; dispatch/fleet/remediate1.json's `asked` says the same; board-requests/remediate1.md repeats it. Tracker [issue.74] (the pre-existing FIST/FISTP issue at the same site) carries 'ROUTED TO lane.remote -- target/** is theirs, the same routing #67 took'.
remediation: See pass-2 finding P1: the routing is declared but was never delivered. lane.remote's brief (dispatch/fleet/remote.json, dispatched 2026-09-14T05:23:05Z, 30 minutes BEFORE pass 1 landed at 05:53:29Z) names neither M2 nor M4 nor #74, and pass1.json carries no owner field on any record.

summary: pgraph_vk_get_clear_color() now derives the pad-alpha stamp from pgraph_vk_surface_drawn_format(r->color_binding), falling back to the register only when no colour binding exists. Structural, as the pass1_overstated field predicted; no pixel change, and none was expected or found.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- the clear and the sampler answering 'which constant do this surface's pad bits carry' from two different pieces of state -- can no longer occur. Both sides now read the same SurfaceBinding.
evidence: The load-bearing claim was checked at the source rather than taken from the commit message. On the create path (surface.c:3119-3123) target->drawn_format, target->fmt and target->host_fmt are assigned adjacently from the same target; on the compatible-reuse path (surface.c:3340-3342) surface->drawn_format, surface->fmt and surface->host_fmt are assigned together from the same target. So a binding cannot report one format to the clear and another to the sampler. Separately verified that the two DERIVATIONS agree, which the commit does not claim and which the fix silently depends on: pgraph_glsl_surface_pad_alpha_mode() (psh.c:187-199) returns ZERO for X1R5G5B5_Z/X8R8G8B8_Z, ONE for the _O twins and NONE otherwise, and kelvin_surface_color_format_vk_map (constants.h:497+) carries SWIZZLE_ZERO/SWIZZLE_ONE on exactly those four entries, with X1A7R8G8B8_{Z,O} deliberately left without an override on both sides. No-binding fallback is unreachable for all three callers: draw.c:6509, 6599 and 6604 all sit inside `if (write_color && r->color_binding)`. No behavioural change confirmed: all three call sites are inside pgraph_vk_clear_surface() (draw.c:6367), whose pgraph_vk_surface_update() at 6396 precedes them, so register and binding hold the same value at every reachable call.
remediation: None required for the finding. Pass 1's suggested route was 'resolve the clear stamp through surface->host_fmt like the sampler does'; the fix instead reads binding->drawn_format, a sibling field of the same struct refreshed by the same assignments. Equivalent for the named scenario and better typed -- drawn_format is the guest format enum the pad-mode helper already takes, where host_fmt.sampled_pad_alpha is a VkComponentSwizzle. Recording it as taking a slightly different route than pass 1 proposed.
note: Pass 1's overstatement is confirmed as overstatement: psh.c:180-186's 'a binding reused across a format change reports whichever format first created it' is contradicted by surface.c:3340-3342 in this tree. The correction stands. A residual that neither pass recorded: the pad-alpha fact is still encoded twice, as a switch in glsl/psh.c and as a column in vk/constants.h. They agree at HEAD for all ten colour formats -- I checked each -- but nothing enforces it, and M3 was a two-sources-of-truth finding. Logged as pass-2 finding P4 at LOW.

summary: Correctly out of lane.remediate1's scope: hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/*.c is lane.remote's territory in territory.toml wave 39. Recorded in the same four places as M2.
scenario: Not verified as closed; no code change was made. The unconditional android_log_texture_stage_errors() on the !surf_to_tex path is still there. Confirmed NOT silently dropped, by the same records that cover M2.

summary: The one facility in scope -- the #54 VRAM-race probe -- is behind HAKUX_VRAM_RACE_PROBE, default 0, and compiles out completely. The two deferred facilities are verified as correctly deferred rather than dropped, but the removal-plan half of pass 1's remediation was not delivered.
scenario: Pass 1's named cost scenario -- an RCU read plus a dirty-bitmap scan on every vertex-range copy in sync_vertex_ram_buffer and on every begin_pre_draw window, unswitchable, so a later timing run measures the probe -- can no longer occur. With the flag off begin_pre_draw() is begin_pre_draw_inner() and nothing else.
evidence: Compile-out verified by grep rather than by reading the diff: every reference to g_hakux_vram_race (draw.c:139, 197, 207, 4024, 4028, 4043, 6303, 6306) and to vram_range_dirty_checked (190, 4036, 4040, 6304) sits inside a `#if HAKUX_VRAM_RACE_PROBE` region. The only cross-file symbol is hakux_vram_race_snprintf, declared in renderer.h:1697 and called from pgraph/profile.c:564-567; it is defined in both arms of the #if/#else with the same signature, so switching the probe off needs no edit in profile.c, which is not this lane's territory. In the OFF arm of begin_pre_draw() the local `r` is not declared, so there is no unused-variable exposure; in sync_vertex_ram_buffer `r` is used unconditionally elsewhere (draw.c:6250, 6257). Default-off build verified by compiling (see pass2.md); the -DHAKUX_VRAM_RACE_PROBE=1 build was NOT independently rebuilt here and rests on inspection plus the commit's claim.
remediation: The removal plans pass 1 asked to be recorded on the owning issues were missing when I verified this, and were DELIVERED WHILE PASS 2 WAS IN FLIGHT by 197785e142, which landed on the branch tip mid-audit. [issue.43].blocked_on and [issue.54].blocked_on now both open with a RETIREMENT CONDITION paragraph, and docs/audits/2026-09-14-decisions.md logs the orchestrator's decision on M5's third facility, the accel/tcg/ counters. Re-verified after rebasing onto it: HAKUX_VRAM_RACE_PROBE now occurs in nv2a_issues.toml. M5 is complete. See pass-2 finding P3 for the sequence.
note: The #43 deferral reasoning was checked against the tracker's actual text as it stood BEFORE 197785e142 added the retirement paragraph, and HOLDS. [issue.43].blocked_on reads, verbatim: 'THE DECIDING INSTRUMENT counts uniform STAGINGS rather than pass requests ... with three registered outcomes: staged_high == 0 ... staged_high == folds ... and 0 < staged_high < folds ... Registered VOID on silence.' A default-off flag produces that silence, so flagging the [signfold] counters would convert a live registered measurement into a void one rather than make it cheaper. One qualification the commit does not state: #43's blocked_on names the instrument by behaviour (staged_high/folds) and never contains the string 'signfold'; the binding to the [signfold] log tag lives in docs/testing/predictions/signed-blend-ring0-diagnostic-v2.json, whose R1 leg reads 'VOID, NOT PASSED, if no [signfold] line appears at all.' The reasoning is sound; its authority is the prediction file as much as the tracker. The same prediction file records an earlier arm that came back VOID for exactly this reason, which is direct evidence that the silence failure is real and not hypothetical. The third facility, the TCG counters in accel/tcg/, is genuinely in nobody's claim (accel/** is [free]) and was correctly filed as a board request rather than edited; that request is also unanswered.

summary: GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE's comment calls lineParams.w 'unused'; it is lineTieBias. Identical stale text in vk/shaders.c:38.
scenario: Unchanged at HEAD. A later edit that trusts 'unused' and repurposes lineParams.w destroys the tie break.
remediation: Correct both comments to name the fourth component. Two lines of comment text, no code risk. vk/draw.c and vk/shaders.c are lane.remediate1's.
evidence: Both texts verified present verbatim at draw.c:897-906 and shaders.c:36-50. The third copy, glsl/geom.c:206-217, is the correct one ('one rasteriser subpixel quantum in guest px'), and geom.c:224 has '#define lineTieBias lineParams.w'. The producer side names it too: draw.c:2452-2456 computes out[3] under a comment calling it 'the wide line's low-open tie-break'. So three comments describe one vec4 and two of them are wrong. Requested because a comment that is factually wrong is worse than no comment, and this one is the stated KEEP-IN-SYNC contract for three files.

summary: GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE defined independently in draw.c:906 and shaders.c:50; the widening predicate exists as geom_widens_lines() (draw.c:915) and as widen_lines (glsl/geom.c:124).
scenario: No current defect. A future edit to one copy is a silent wrong-topology or wrong-offset bug.
remediation: Not fixed, because: all four copies were re-checked at HEAD and still agree (the macros are character-identical; the predicates differ only by geom.c's `opts.vulkan &&` term, which is always true on the path draw.c serves); each site already carries an explicit KEEP-IN-SYNC comment that correctly names the hazard; and the proposed fix -- a shared header plus exporting the predicate from glsl/geom.h -- crosses into glsl/, which serves the GL renderer as well and is not this lane's to restructure. Recommended as a fold-in for whichever change next touches the geometry push contract, rather than as a standalone edit.
evidence: Verified all four at HEAD. The duplication's reach has grown since pass 1: GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE now has six uses in draw.c and four in shaders.c, one of which (shaders.c:836) writes the value into a persisted cache key -- see L8.

summary: The one-shot wide-line diagnostic keys `static uint32_t last_bits` on subPixelPrecisionBits alone, but also prints surface_scale_factor and the derived tie bias.
scenario: The guest changes resolution, surface_scale_factor moves, out[3] moves with it, and the log still shows the first value.
remediation: Key the one-shot on out[3], or on the (bits, surface_scale_factor) pair. One expression.
evidence: Verified unchanged at draw.c:2477-2502. Worse than pass 1 recorded in one detail: `bits` is the CLAMPED value (draw.c:2452-2455 forces 8 when the device reports 0 or >16), so the key is even less able to move than the raw limit. Requested rather than deferred because the comment immediately above this code is itself about a diagnostic that 'reads as having been checked' -- the same failure one level up -- and because the Android branch visibly prints scale as part of the payload.

summary: The staging comment says the renderer 'leaves the selector at LOW'; pgraph_vk_flush_draw resets it to SIGNED_BLEND_PASS_NONE.
scenario: No runtime effect. It misstates the invariant a reader would use to reason about whether an unfolded draw can stage a fold.
remediation: One word, LOW -> NONE. glsl/psh.c is NOT lane.remediate1's territory, so this is routed via board-requests/audit2.md together with the separate psh.c:180-186 staleness that board-requests/remediate1.md section 5 already raised. Both are comment-only corrections in the same file and should go as one grant.
evidence: Verified contradictory at HEAD: psh.c:3573-3582 still says LOW; draw.c:7519-7524 calls pgraph_glsl_set_signed_blend_pass(SIGNED_BLEND_PASS_NONE) under a comment saying 'a selector that says low half outside a fold is a lie waiting to be believed'. The code below the stale comment is itself correct and does not rely on the asserted invariant.

summary: `#define floatx80_round` retained as an alias for round-to-integer, where softfloat's floatx80_round rounds to the control word's PRECISION.
scenario: A future caller in this file compiles cleanly and gets silently wrong semantics; deleting the macro would make such a caller a hard compile error instead.
remediation: Delete the floatx80_round macro; keep floatx80_round_to_int. Verified to be a pure subtraction: there are ZERO callers of floatx80_round anywhere in target/i386/. target/** is lane.remote's.
evidence: Repo-wide check: the real definition is fpu/softfloat.c:5354 and include/fpu/softfloat.h:968; the only callers are thirteen sites in target/m68k/fpu_helper.c, a different translation unit that this file's #define cannot reach. So the macro is dead today and its deletion cannot break any build.

summary: The `default:` arm uses rint(), which follows the host FP environment, leaning on 'which QEMU never changes'.
scenario: Any code in the process that sets the host rounding mode on the vCPU thread silently changes guest FRNDINT results in the nearest case only.
remediation: Not fixed, because the assumption was independently re-verified repo-wide at HEAD and holds: fesetround/fegetround appear only in tests/ (tests/tcg/multiarch, tests/tcg/arm, tests/fp/fp-bench.c), fenv.h is included nowhere outside tests/, and every FPCR/FPSCR hit is guest register emulation or a disassembler table -- no host-FPCR write, no _controlfp, no __builtin_flt_rounds. The residual exposure is to third-party libraries loaded at runtime, which this tree cannot see or enforce. The proposed fix (roundeven, or nearbyint under an asserted mode) is a behavioural change on a hot guest path in lane.remote's territory and belongs with M2's rounding work, not as a standalone edit. Routed as a note on M2 rather than as its own request.
evidence: Grep evidence recorded above; the finding's own claim was re-tested rather than inherited.

summary: floor/ceil/trunc/rint raise nothing into s->float_exception_flags, so FRNDINT never sets PE, though helper_frndint brackets the call with save/merge_exception_flags as if it did.
scenario: A guest that unmasks the precision exception takes no #MF where hardware does. nxdk leaves PM masked.
remediation: Not fixed here -- target/** is lane.remote's -- and the finding is BROADER than pass 1 recorded, so it is escalated as pass-2 finding P2 rather than closed as a LOW. merge_exception_flags() is `#ifndef USE_HARD_FPU` and therefore an EMPTY FUNCTION on the whole hard-FPU path, so no x87 status-word exception bit is ever raised by any helper there, not only PE from FRNDINT. That also makes pass 1's own M2 remediation only half-effective as written; see P2.
evidence: Verified at fpu_helper.c:722-734 (merge_exception_flags body entirely inside #ifndef USE_HARD_FPU) and fpu_helper.c:189/358 (the native-double block is inside #ifdef USE_HARD_FPU). save_exception_flags (715-720) still runs and still clears the flags to 0. fpu_helper.c is compiled twice (fpu_helper_hard.c:2 defines USE_HARD_FPU 1) with runtime dispatch via MAP_HELPER_SOFT_HARD, and on aarch64 the __hard helpers use native double -- so this is the live path on the Android target. The softfloat build is unaffected and retains correct PE behaviour.

summary: SHADER_STATE_LAYOUT_VERSION is still 1 though PshState gained bool tex_comp0_const[4], and the file's comment requires a manual bump when a field changes without changing any size.
scenario: Pass 1's feared case: if sizeof did not move, shader_module_keys.bin survives the upgrade and is reinterpreted with a field that used to be padding, giving an assertion inside shader generation during warmup.
remediation: The feared scenario is REFUTED and needs no fix; the residual gap is real and is what is requested: add sizeof(ShaderModuleCacheKey) to the fingerprint at renderer.c:98-101, so the GenVshGlslOptions / GenGeomGlslOptions / GenPshGlslOptions structs are covered. A version bump is now a no-op for correctness.
evidence: Refuted empirically, not by reading the struct: compiling the before/after PshState prefix gives sizeof 180 -> 184 and moves tex_signed from offset 164 to 168. bool[4] at offset 157-160 leaves 3 padding bytes before a 4-aligned uint32_t[4], and the new bool[4] needs 4, so it consumed the padding plus one byte and grew the struct. Both weighted sizeof terms in the stamp therefore changed and the cache was wiped automatically on the first run of the new build; the reinterpretation pass 1 feared cannot have happened. (Computed on x86-64; bool is 1 byte and uint32_t 4-aligned on aarch64 too, so the arithmetic is identical on the target.) The residual is separate and still open: the stamp sizeofs only ShaderState, PshState and VshState, while shader_module_key_persist() (shaders.c:998-1013) fwrites a whole ShaderModuleCacheKey -- which embeds GenVshGlslOptions -- to disk. GenVshGlslOptions is not covered by any term, and its vertex_push_offset changed from 0 to 16 in this window (shaders.c:836). This time the PshState size change wiped that file too, by luck rather than by design.

summary: A zero-length line now emits nothing, where the line_strip path emitted a degenerate line primitive. The justification is a claim about silicon, not a derivation from the goldens.
scenario: A title that draws zero-length lines as a point-plotting idiom loses them. Whether hardware lights a pixel there is not established and the corpus is not stated to contain the case.
remediation: Not fixed as code, because the early return is required -- l2 is the divisor at geom.c:408-411 -- so there is no correct alternative to write without a measurement first. The right output is a record, not an edit: filed in board-requests/audit2.md as an assumption to note on #13 together with the capture that would settle it. Changing the behaviour on either side of an unmeasured question would be the guess the finding objects to.
evidence: Verified unchanged at geom.c:404-407. The asymmetry the finding names is real and visible: the three adjacent modelling choices at geom.c:412-443 each carry explicit golden counts (4.562%, 1,911 of 41,892, the 1/512-1/64 bias ladder), and this one carries a bare assertion.

summary: max_vertices for PRIM_TYPE_TRIANGLES + POLY_MODE_LINE doubled from 6 to 12; nothing asserts maxGeometryOutputVertices or maxGeometryTotalOutputComponents.
scenario: A device at the Vulkan guaranteed minimum with a larger varying set fails to compile the geometry shader, and in this renderer a failed shader compile is a silent 'draws nothing', not a build error.
remediation: Assert both geometry limits once at device init, alongside the subPixelPrecisionBits log that this window already added. The most substantive of the twelve LOWs and the only one whose scenario is a silent wrong picture on real hardware.
evidence: Verified at geom.c:139-153 (12 present) and by repo-wide grep: maxGeometryOutputVertices and maxGeometryTotalOutputComponents appear in exactly three places -- two VkPhysicalDeviceLimits field declarations in the bundled SDL2 vulkan_core.h, and pass1.json's own text. Nothing in hw/ or ui/ reads either limit. The nearest comparable check on this path, the subPixelPrecisionBits handling at draw.c:2452-2455, is a silent clamp rather than an assert.

summary: At exactly |dx| == |dy| the `ad.x >= ad.y` test picks the y axis for the tie bias arbitrarily; which axis silicon treats as minor at 45 degrees is not derived.
scenario: Only band edges landing exactly on a pixel centre on an exactly-45-degree line can move.
remediation: Not fixed as code -- the remediation pass 1 asked for is itself comment-only ('note that the 45-degree case is a tie the goldens do not separate'), and it belongs with L9 in the same geom.c comment pass and the same #13 note. Bundled there rather than requested separately.
evidence: Verified at geom.c:444-445. Both of the finding's sub-claims check out: max(ad.x, ad.y) + 0.5 * min(ad.x, ad.y) (geom.c:409-411) is symmetric under component swap, so the extent n is genuinely unaffected at the tie, and the two tie vectors have equal magnitude lineTieBias -- only the direction flips. The 32-line justification block above it covers the band choice and the bias magnitude in detail and says nothing about the axis, which is exactly the asymmetry recorded.

summary: The partial-clear path, which clears by drawing with vkCmdSetBlendConstants, also carries the pad-alpha stamp. Whether silicon writes the format's pad bits on a CLEAR_SURFACE that does not enable the alpha channel is not derived.
scenario: A guest that issues CLEAR_SURFACE with the colour bits but not the alpha bit on an X8R8G8B8_{Z,O} surface: we either stamp the pad byte when hardware leaves it, or leave it when hardware stamps it.
remediation: Not fixed, because both available edits are guesses at the same unmeasured question -- restricting the stamp to full clears is as underived as applying it to partial ones, and Clear::TestSurfaceFmt, the capture the stamp rests on, clears all channels and cannot separate them. Recorded as a gap on #59 via board-requests/audit2.md, naming the capture that would close it, which is the finding's own first option.
evidence: Verified still applied at HEAD: the partial branch (draw.c:6602-6607) calls the same pgraph_vk_get_clear_color() as the full branch, with no full-vs-partial gate. Confirmed the partial path is the only clear route that by construction does not write all four channels -- the inline fast path at draw.c:6470-6472 excludes partial colour clears explicitly. The M3 remediation changed this function's state source in this window but does not touch the full-vs-partial question.

summary: M2 and M4 are routed to lane.remote in four records, but lane.remote was never told, and the authoritative audit record names the wrong findings. pass1.md's 'For pass 2' paragraph reads 'M2 and M3 touch files another lane holds (vk/texture.c) or shared guest-CPU code' -- it means M2 and M4, and M4's file is gl/texture.c, not vk/texture.c. M3 was remediated in place and was never a routing case.
scenario: The protocol's failure mode for a routed finding. A reader reconciling the audit against the remediation set sees M1, M3 and M5 fixed and M2/M3 named as routed, so M4 appears in no list at all and drops silently -- which is precisely the outcome the two-pass rule exists to prevent. pass1.json carries no owner, lane or routing field on any of its 18 records, so nothing machine-readable contradicts the prose.
remediation: Correct pass1.md:297 to say M2 and M4, with gl/texture.c as M4's file. Deliver both findings to lane.remote: its brief (dispatch/fleet/remote.json, dispatched 2026-09-14T05:23:05Z) was issued 30 minutes BEFORE pass 1 landed (945ed9d60f, 05:53:29Z), its `asked` string names neither finding, and its issues list omits #74 -- the tracker entry that itself says 'ROUTED TO lane.remote'. M4 additionally has no tracker entry of any kind: nv2a_issues.toml has no hit for gl/texture, glGetError, download_overlap or android_log_texture_stage_errors. Filed in board-requests/audit2.md.

summary: merge_exception_flags() is wrapped in `#ifndef USE_HARD_FPU`, so on the hard-FPU path it is an empty function. No x87 status-word exception bit -- IE, ZE, OE, UE, PE, DE -- is ever raised by any helper on that path, not only PE from FRNDINT as pass 1's L7 recorded. Every helper on that path still brackets its work with save_exception_flags/merge_exception_flags, so the code reads as though it maintains the status word.
scenario: A guest that reads the x87 status word after an operation -- FNSTSW, or FSTENV -- sees the exception bits permanently clear, and a guest that unmasks any of them takes no #MF where hardware does. This is the live path on the Android target: fpu_helper.c is compiled twice (fpu_helper_hard.c:2 defines USE_HARD_FPU 1) with runtime dispatch through MAP_HELPER_SOFT_HARD, and on aarch64 the __hard helpers use native double. nxdk leaves the exception masks set, so nothing in the corpus is known to reach it.
remediation: Route to lane.remote with M2, and correct M2's remediation before it is executed. M2 as written says to 'set float_flag_invalid on out-of-range and NaN so the existing guards in helper_fist*_ST0 become live'. That half works -- helper_fistl_ST0's guard at fpu_helper.c:911 reads get_float_exception_flags() DIRECTLY and does not go through merge_exception_flags, so the integer-indefinite 0x80000000 would be stored correctly. But the other half does not: the guest's status word would still never show IE, because merge_exception_flags is compiled out. Whoever takes M2 should either restore the status-word merge on the hard path or state, at the top of the USE_HARD_FPU block, that x87 exception flags are deliberately out of scope for it -- which is L7's second option, now known to apply to the whole block rather than to one function. Note the file already carries a bare 'FIXME: rounding and exceptions' at fpu_helper.c:391 for the x86_64 variant of the same class.
